subject: Discovery: embeddings & reranking for site search - recap and next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T14:03:00Z
Subject: Discovery: embeddings + rerank for site search

Hi Marissa -

Thanks for taking time to speak with us tomorrow. Quick context so we can use the meeting efficiently:

- What we do: Acme Retail runs product search across web and mobile (approx 12M SKUs).
- Current infra: Postgres for product metadata + Elasticsearch for keyword search. We are piloting vector search for semantic relevance; currently testing Pinecone (managed) with 512-d embeddings generated offline.
- Traffic: steady-state ~30 qps, peak ~120 qps on promotions. Nightly rerank batch that processes ~200k queries for personalization/merch tasks.
- Pain: Elasticsearch relevance is brittle for long-tail queries and queries with attributes. Vector approach improved recall but costs/latency are concerns.
- Targets: p50 latency <=150ms for interactive queries, p95 <=300ms; cost goal ~<$0.50 per 1k queries for inference+vector lookup. Success metrics: precision@10, CTR lift on recommendations, and 10% reduction in site search drop-offs.

Agenda for our call: discovery of current stack, expected SLAs, indexing cadence, sample dataset, and POC scope.

Jordan
Senior Product Manager
Acme Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-09-11T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery: embeddings + rerank for site search

Hi Jordan / Priya -

Great to meet earlier - thanks for walking through the use case. Below is a concise recap from our discussion plus proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Summary of what you told us
- Current stack: Postgres + Elasticsearch for primary search; experimenting with Pinecone for vector search. Embeddings currently generated offline (512-d) using a vendor model.
- Index scale: ~12M product vectors; average vector size 512 dims; incremental refreshs daily with full reindex weekly.
- Query patterns: 30 qps baseline, peak ~120 qps; interactive queries are latency-sensitive (target p50 <=150ms, p95 <=300ms).
- Batch workloads: nightly/midnight rerank jobs that run large scoring passes (100k-250k queries) for merchandising personalization; these are throughput-oriented and can be batched.
- Pain points: (a) maintaining low latency at scale with vector lookups + reranking, (b) cost predictability for high-query volumes, (c) integration complexity across ranked pipelines (ES + vector store + model scoring).
- Success criteria: precision@10 improvement vs baseline, uplift in CTR for promoted results, and meeting latency/cost targets above.

What Redwood recommends as a POC scope (high level)
1) Technical deep-dive (2h): include Dev Patel and your infra engineer to map traffic patterns, secrets/keys, and network requirements. 
2) POC: 2-week scoped run using a 1-2M vector sample (representative shard) to validate latency & cost under realistic QPS/batch loads. We'll test both online vector lookup + in-place rerank and batched rerank flows.
3) Metrics & evaluation: we'll measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/cost per query for any model scoring, and ranking metrics (precision@10 / MRR).
4) Deliverables: runbook for scaling to 12M vectors, recommended quantization/replication config, and a cost model for operational estimates.

Assumptions / open questions
- Embeddings: are you able to share a 1-2M vector sample (S3 preferred) or a small anonymized export?
- Vector DB: confirm if Pinecone is locked in or if you're open to alternatives (e.g., RedisAI/RedisVector, Milvus, or managed backends).
- Security/Compliance: any data residency or SOC2 evidence we should prep before a POC?

Next steps
- Jordan/Priya: share a sample dataset (S3 link or export) + preferred time for a 2h technical deep-dive this week.
- I'll loop in Dev Patel (cc'd) to cover runtime/integration questions.
- We'll prepare a proposed POC plan and cost estimate within 48 hours after the deep dive.

Attachments: redwood_discovery_notes.pdf (high-level notes + proposed POC outline)

Thanks - looking forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa - this is exactly what we needed. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can provide a 1.5M-vector sample in S3 (anonymized IDs + vectors + a few attributes) by end of day Wednesday.
- Pinecone is what our ML team has been trialing but we are not locked in - interested to see Redwood's guidance on tradeoffs.
- Nightly rerank cadence is 03:00 UTC and currently processes ~180k queries (more during Black Friday windows). Those are batch jobs run on a separate cluster; latency isn't critical for them but throughput/cost is.
- Security: we are SOC2 in progress; for POC we can share sanitized data and a gov-acct for access.

I attached a quick screenshot of our current vector index config (acme_current_stack_screenshot.png).

For the technical deep-dive, Friday 2026-09-12 16:00 PT works for our infra lead. I booked that slot on the Calendly you sent.

Jordan
